intended_object: The defining Hopf ideal, inside the coordinate Hopf algebra of the subgroup of GL₂₄ generated by the tripled D₄ root subgroups and weight torus, of the smallest closed subgroup scheme containing the four positive simple-root subgroups and the rank-four weight torus. This reading comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
`commonKernelHopfIdeal f` is the supremum of all Hopf ideals that lie in the kernel of every map `f i`. So it is the largest Hopf ideal killed by all the generator maps, and the lemma `le_commonKernelHopfIdeal_iff` states this characterization. In scheme terms, closed subgroup schemes correspond to Hopf ideals with the order reversed, so this ideal cuts out the smallest closed subgroup through which every generator morphism factors. That is the closed subgroup generated by the given subgroups, as in Milne §2.h.

The family `generator` sends `.inl i` to the lifts of the four root subgroups indexed by `.inl (.inl i)`, the positive numbered roots, and sends `.inr ()` to the weight-torus lift. This matches the docstring.

The ring `A` is an arbitrary commutative ring, so there is no unnecessary restriction. The object is a specific one tied to the tripled D₄ representation, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no general counterpart, because it lacks Hopf ideals and closed subgroup schemes in this sense.
